fixes.explanation: Strengthen is the word, baker, and the verse says it first. The LORD says, “I will strengthen you; I will surely help you; I will uphold you with My righteous right hand.” (Isaiah 41:10). Strength, help and upholding all come in one breath. Hard to ask for a better promise.

Desert is the one, baker. The LORD says, “I will turn the desert into a pool of water, and the dry land into flowing springs.” (Isaiah 41:18). A desert becomes a pool of water. The dry land gets flowing springs too, and that's quite a change.

Firstborn sounds official, friend, but it isn't what the LORD says here. He says, “…descendant of Abraham My friend—” (Isaiah 41:8). Firstborn would be about rank, and “friend” is about closeness. I think that's a better title than any rank.

City isn't in that verse, baker. The LORD says, “I will turn the desert into a pool of water…” (Isaiah 41:18). Nothing in that line turns a city into anything. The dry places are where the water goes.
